name: Mini International Personality Item Pool
domain: Self talk, thinking patterns and personality
construct: Big Five personality factors measured with 20 public domain IPIP items, 4 per factor.
licence: Because the IPIP has been placed in the public domain, permission has already been automatically granted for any person to use IPIP items, scales, and inventories for any purpose, commercial or non-commercial.
instructions: Below are phrases describing people's behaviors. Please use the rating scale below to describe how accurately each statement describes you. Describe yourself as you generally are now, not as you wish to be in the future. Describe yourself as you honestly see yourself, in relation to other people you know of the same sex as you are, and roughly your same age. Please read each statement carefully, and put a number from 1 to 5 next to it to describe how accurately the statement describes you.

items.text: Am the life of the party.
Am not interested in other people's problems.
Often forget to put things back in their proper place.
Am relaxed most of the time.
Am not interested in abstract ideas.
Talk to a lot of different people at parties.
Am not really interested in others.
Do not have a good imagination.

subscales.name: Extraversion
subscales.description: IPIP Factor I, Surgency or Extraversion; alpha .77 on the key page.

subscales.name: Neuroticism
subscales.description: IPIP Factor IV; Emotional Stability scored in reverse and labelled Neuroticism; alpha .68.

subscales.name: Intellect or Imagination
subscales.description: IPIP Factor V, often labelled Openness; alpha .65.

scoring: Reverse the minus keyed items (6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20) by subtracting the response from 6, then sum the 4 items for each factor, giving a range of 4 to 20 per factor. Higher scores indicate more of the trait; for Neuroticism a higher score indicates less emotional stability. No cut offs; the scales are normative trait measures.
citation: Donnellan, M. B., Oswald, F. L., Baird, B. M., & Lucas, R. E. (2006). The Mini-IPIP scales: Tiny-yet-effective measures of the Big Five factors of personality. Psychological Assessment, 18(2), 192–203. https://doi.org/10.1037/1040-3590.18.2.192
transcriptionNote: Item text, factor membership and plus or minus keying transcribed from the IPIP Mini-IPIP key page, which gives no item numbers, instructions or response labels. Item order 1 to 20, the standard IPIP instructions and the 5 response labels were taken from the LibreTexts reproduction of the Donnellan et al. (2006) Mini-IPIP (CC BY-NC-SA page; items themselves public domain); that ordering matches the factor and reverse keying pattern of the Millisecond Mini-IPIP manual (item 1 E, 2 A, 3 C, 4 N, 5 I, 6 E reversed, and so on). Item wording is identical across the IPIP key and LibreTexts. Factor V is named Intellect or Imagination on the IPIP key and Openness on LibreTexts.
